column1: Tone: The FOMC statement is mildly positive on growth and the labor market but acknowledges weakening business investment, soft exports, and muted inflation with elevated uncertainties. The July 2019 SLOOS adds a more cautious credit backdrop: banks reported tightening standards for C&I loans and tighter terms across firm sizes, weaker demand for construction and land development loans, and some tightening in CRE, alongside mixed signals (some reports of easier standards) and generally unchanged demand for certain consumer loans. There was also reported willingness to lend in some consumer categories and stronger demand for government loans, but overall the SLOOS points to tighter credit supply and softer loan demand where business investment is most sensitive. Taken together, the SLOOS tempers the mildly positive tone of the statement, tilting sentiment closer to neutral with downside risk from tighter financing conditions for firms. sentiment score = 0.08
